title: State of Maharashtra v. Cosmos Co-operative Bank Malware Syndicate
crime_type: Cyber Malware Heist / ATM Switch Cloned Transactions / Global SWIFT Attack
court_or_authority: Sessions Court, Pune / Cyber Crime Police Station Pune
legal_citation: Regular Criminal Case No. 4882/2019; Cyber FIR No. 22/2018
source: Pune Cyber Crime Police Charge-sheet & Indian Kanoon
ipc_sections: Section 468 IPC (Forgery for purpose of cheating)
Section 471 IPC (Using forged document as genuine)
evidence: Injection of custom proxy malware into Cosmos Bank ATM payment switch server in Pune, bypassing CBS authorization
Simultaneous coordinated withdrawals totaling ₹78 crore across 14,000 ATM transactions in 28 countries within 2 hours
Malicious SWIFT message transmissions siphoning ₹13.9 crore to bank accounts in Hong Kong
Seizure of cloned magnetic strip debit cards and cash from domestic money mules in Pune and Mumbai
modus_operandi: Infiltrated the cooperative bank internal network via targeted spear-phishing emails containing malware. Severed the connection between the bank ATM switch and its Core Banking System (CBS), deploying a malicious proxy server that auto-approved withdrawal requests for cloned debit cards worldwide during a banking holiday weekend.
personality_disorder: Coordinated cyber warfare, militaristic discipline, compartmentalized criminal hierarchy, and complete emotional detachment.
common_traits: Spear-phishing delivery of zero-day switch malware
Decoupling payment gateway from Core Banking verification
Exploitation of long holiday weekends to delay detection
summary: Historic ₹94 crore cyber heist striking Cosmos Bank in August 2018. Highlighted critical infrastructure vulnerabilities in Indian banking switches and resulted in definitive RBI cybersecurity directives for urban cooperative banks.
